claims.text: The initial material is a MoSi2 coating on a Mo-based alloy substrate.
Hf and Al2O3 can be co-doped into a MoSi2 coating to form a (Mo,Hf)Si2-Al2O3 composite coating.
Adding Hf and Al2O3 to a MoSi2 coating improves its high-temperature oxygen resistance relative to an undoped MoSi2 coating.
The co-doped coating is intended to resist oxidation at 1400 °C in static air.
Oxidation of the co-doped coating forms an oxide scale containing HfO2, SiO2, and mullite.
The oxide scale becomes relatively dense and protective as oxidation proceeds.
The dense oxide scale limits oxidation by controlling oxygen permeation through the scale.
Formation of the protective scale decreases the coating's mass-gain rate.
After 40 h at 1400 °C in static air, the co-doped coating will have a lower mass-gain rate than an undoped MoSi2 coating.
MoSi2 suffers rapid pesting oxidation between 400 and 600 °C, which can disintegrate the material.
The exact synthetic reactions among Al2O3, HfO2, and SiO2 are not fully understood.
Mass change, phase composition, morphology, and elemental distribution can be assessed by gravimetry, XRD, SEM, and EDS during oxidation testing.

contradictions.description: The stated operating and test condition is 1400 °C, whereas the boundary is given as 400–600 °C. If the boundary is meant to define the range in which the intervention should work, it conflicts with the hypothesis and experiment; if it is only background about pesting, it is mislabeled as a boundary.
